pointers.sentence: The insert then leaves the column out where no other row of a bulk insert gives it a value and it is not the only column left, and otherwise writes `"DEFAULT"`, or the default's expression where the backend lacks that keyword (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field._get_default`, `django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLInsertCompiler.as_sql`).

The insert then leaves the column out where no other row of a bulk insert gives it a value and it is not the only column left, and otherwise writes `"DEFAULT"`, or the default's expression where the backend lacks that keyword (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field._get_default`, `django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLInsertCompiler.as_sql`).
`GeneratedField` (5.0) is a column the database computes from its row, and no save writes it (`django/db/models/fields/generated.py:GeneratedField`).
Since 5.2 a constraint over one can be validated (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._get_field_expression_map`).

Since 6.1 PostgreSQL from 18 may have a virtual one and Oracle from 23.7 a stored one; each had had only the other kind (`django/db/backends/postgresql/features.py:DatabaseFeatures.supports_virtual_generated_columns`, `django/db/backends/oracle/features.py:DatabaseFeatures.supports_stored_generated_columns`).

Since 6.1 PostgreSQL from 18 may have a virtual one and Oracle from 23.7 a stored one; each had had only the other kind (`django/db/backends/postgresql/features.py:DatabaseFeatures.supports_virtual_generated_columns`, `django/db/backends/oracle/features.py:DatabaseFeatures.supports_stored_generated_columns`).
After an update it also asks for the generated fields that depend on a field it writes (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._save_table`).
Under 5.2.17 on SQLite a generated column was right after an insert but stale after an update, so on SQLite the 6.0 notes' "now refreshed" is new for it only on an update (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`).

Where the backend cannot return columns, as on MySQL, and on MariaDB after an update, the field is instead removed from the instance and so deferred to the next read (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._assign_returned_values`; [Saving an instance](../models/saving.md#what-comes-back)).

Since 6.0 the insert of a save that is not raw calls `django.db.models.Field.pre_save` twice for each field it writes: in `_save_table`, to see if the value is an expression, and in the compiler (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._save_table`, `django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLInsertCompiler.pre_save_val`).

Since 6.0 the insert of a save that is not raw calls `django.db.models.Field.pre_save` twice for each field it writes: in `_save_table`, to see if the value is an expression, and in the compiler (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._save_table`, `django/db/models/sql/compiler.py:SQLInsertCompiler.pre_save_val`).

Under `CASCADE` the collector deletes the related rows itself, and fetches them first where a receiver of `pre_delete` or `post_delete` must be called, or their own relations followed (`django/db/models/deletion.py:Collector.can_fast_delete`).
6.1 added three `DatabaseOnDelete` values that leave the work to the `ON DELETE` clause the schema editor writes (`django/db/models/deletion.py:DatabaseOnDelete`).
They are in `SKIP_COLLECTION` with `DO_NOTHING`, so a delete's collector passes the relation over (`django/db/models/deletion.py:Collector.collect`).
The 6.1 notes give the saved fetch as the reason, and the unsent signals as its consequence (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).
The checks refuse a key with one of the database's actions to a model whose own key has one of the collector's, or the reverse (`django/db/models/fields/related.py:ForeignKey._check_on_delete`).
`Collector.delete` sends `post_delete` only for the rows it collected, and counts only those (`django/db/models/deletion.py:Collector.delete`).
`CompositePrimaryKey` (5.2) is a field without a column, assigned to `pk`, whose value is a tuple (`django/db/models/fields/composite.py:CompositePrimaryKey`).

It also refused, as `"models.E049"`, a `ForeignObject` given several fields as `from_fields=` and named in an index, a constraint or `Options.unique_together`, which 5.2.17 let pass (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._check_local_fields`).
`Model._is_pk_set` counts a key unset when it is `None` or a tuple with a part unset, and since 6.1 when it holds a `DatabaseDefault` (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._is_pk_set`).
An unsaved instance whose key is unset is now equal only to itself (`django/db/models/base.py:Model.__eq__`; [An instance and its state](../models/instances.md)).
The 6.2 notes say unsaved instances with a composite key "no longer compare equal to other instances" (`docs/releases/6.2.txt`); two with the same whole key still do.
The automatic key's default became `BigAutoField` in 6.0 (`django/conf/global_settings.py`; [What changed](../changes.md#an-old-habit-release-by-release)).
Since 6.0 it raises the model's own `Model.NotUpdated` (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._save_table`).

`ModelBase.__new__` makes it a subclass of a concrete parent's, or else of `ObjectNotUpdated` and `DatabaseError`, which it keeps for backward compatibility (`django/db/models/base.py:ModelBase.__new__`; [`ModelBase`: a class statement becomes a model](../models/metaclass.md)).

The setter of `Field.choices` passes them to `normalize_choices`, which makes the pairs (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.choices`, `django/utils/choices.py:normalize_choices`; [Choices: `normalize_choices` and the choice iterators](../utils/choices.md)).

The setter of `Field.choices` passes them to `normalize_choices`, which makes the pairs (`django/db/models/fields/__init__.py:Field.choices`, `django/utils/choices.py:normalize_choices`; [Choices: `normalize_choices` and the choice iterators](../utils/choices.md)).
`USE_BLANK_CHOICE_DASH` brings the dashes back until Django 2028 (`django/db/models/utils.py:get_blank_choice_label`; [What changed in forms and validators](forms.md)).
The keyword check, deprecated in 5.1, raises a `TypeError` from 6.0 (`django/db/models/constraints.py:CheckConstraint.__init__`).
Since 6.0 `BaseConstraint.check` returns the system check's messages, and `Model._check_constraints` calls it (`django/db/models/base.py:Model._check_constraints`).
Since 5.2 a message given is used, with the code given (`django/db/models/constraints.py:UniqueConstraint.validate`).
The 5.2 notes say the code and the message "are now always used when provided" (`docs/releases/5.2.txt`).
`AlterIndexTogether` stays for old migrations (`django/db/migrations/operations/models.py:AlterIndexTogether`; [Constraints and indexes](../models/constraints.md)).
